question: HbA1c is 8.6% with HFrEF (EF 30%) and CKD 3a. How do I optimize her diabetes regimen given her cardiac status?

drugs_to_avoid.reason: FDA black box - increased HF hospitalization (SAVOR-TIMI)

flags.action: STOP - switch to insulin or Linagliptin
flags.detail: Sulfonylureas accumulate in renal impairment causing prolonged hypoglycemia. RSSDI 2022: STOP sulfonylurea when eGFR <30; use insulin or Linagliptin (no renal adjustment needed).
flags.title: Glimepiride in CKD (eGFR 44): high hypoglycemia risk

flags.action: Monitor K+ at baseline, 1 wk, monthly
flags.detail: Dual RAAS blockade + K-sparing diuretic significantly raises hyperkalemia risk. Current K+ is 5.1 mEq/L. CKD (eGFR 44) compounds the risk. RSSDI+CSI: hold spironolactone if K+ >5.5. Adding SGLT2i mitigates risk.
flags.title: Hyperkalemia risk: Ramipril + Spironolactone

flags.action: Avoid alcohol. If consumed, eat carbs, monitor glucose.
flags.detail: Severe hypoglycemia, disulfiram-like reaction. Mechanism: Additive hypoglycemic effect; alcohol impairs gluconeogenesis.
flags.title: Glimepiride + Alcohol: SEVERE

flags.action: Hold metformin 48h before and after IV contrast if eGFR <60.
flags.detail: Lactic acidosis. Mechanism: Risk of contrast-induced AKI → metformin accumulation → lactic acidosis.
flags.title: Metformin + IV contrast dye: SEVERE

flags.action: Monitor K+ at baseline, 1 week, then monthly. Hold if K+ >5.5.
flags.detail: HYPERKALEMIA (can be fatal). Mechanism: Dual RAAS blockade + K-sparing diuretic.
flags.title: Spironolactone + Ramipril: SEVERE

flags.action: Avoid or hold statin during macrolide course. Use azithromycin instead.
flags.detail: Myopathy, rhabdomyolysis. Mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition → increased statin levels.
flags.title: Atorvastatin + Erythromycin / Clarithromycin: SEVERE

flags.detail: Beta blockers mask the adrenergic symptoms of hypoglycemia (tachycardia, tremor). Patient must use SMBG and recognise non-adrenergic symptoms (sweating, confusion).
flags.title: Glimepiride + Carvedilol: hypoglycemia unawareness

flags.detail: Hypoglycemia unawareness. Mechanism: Beta blockade masks hypoglycemia.
flags.title: Glimepiride + Carvedilol: MODERATE

flags.action: Limit alcohol. Avoid binge drinking. Patient education.
flags.detail: Lactic acidosis, hypoglycemia. Mechanism: Increased lactic acidosis risk; impairs gluconeogenesis.
flags.title: Metformin + Alcohol: MODERATE

flags.action: Increase antidiabetic doses during steroid course. Monitor glucose.
flags.detail: Loss of glycemic control. Mechanism: Steroids cause hyperglycemia.
flags.title: Metformin + Prednisolone / Steroids: MODERATE

flags.action: Monitor K+ and renal function. Hold metformin if dehydrated.
flags.detail: Hyperkalemia, AKI risk in dehydration. Mechanism: Minor risk of hypoglycemia + lactic acidosis if AKI develops.
flags.title: Metformin + Ramipril: MINOR

flags.detail: Empagliflozin (EMPEROR-Reduced) or Dapagliflozin (DAPA-HF) provides dual benefit: glycemia + HF outcomes. RSSDI+CSI 2022 recommend regardless of HbA1c if T2DM + HFrEF.
flags.title: First-line: SGLT2 inhibitor for diabetes + HF

flags.detail: Dapagliflozin (DAPA-CKD) provides renoprotection at eGFR ≥25. ACEi/ARB mandatory if albuminuria.
flags.title: Consider SGLT2 inhibitor for diabetic kidney disease
